question: What should policymakers watch next?

steps.text: I need the latest published headline figures before answering.
I will check the stored briefing notes for what to watch next.

matches.title: What policymakers should watch next
matches.body: Policymakers should watch petrol, electricity, housing, and the cash rate ahead of the average supermarket aisle. Petrol was up 23.6% and added 0.77 points. Transport was up 8.7% and added 0.99 points. Housing was up 5.2% and added 1.14 points. Electricity was up 12.8%. Rents were up 3.6%. The cash rate target is 4.85 percent after 5 rises in 2026. Fruit's shelf jump is real for households but small in the national index.

matches.title: Cash rate path and mortgage pressure
matches.body: The Reserve Bank cash rate target was 4.85 percent on 2026-11-05. It rose 5 times in 2026, from 3.60 percent before the first rise. The 2026-09-30 move to 4.60 percent shows up in the target and the overnight rate; the published change column for that day is blank. Mortgage repayments sit outside the grocery price index. Households can face both a higher cash rate and uneven grocery prices.

matches.title: Meals out versus cooking at home
matches.body: Meals out and takeaway added 0.28 points to the national yearly rise, more than fruit's 0.09 points, because eating out has a much larger weight. Restaurant meals were up 4.1%. Takeaway was up 3.6%.

steps.text: The published figures I need are already in the observations.

In September 2026, overall prices were up 4.3%. Food and drinks were up 3.2% and added 0.56 points to the national yearly rise. Housing was up 5.2% and added 1.14 points. Transport was up 8.7% and added 0.99 points, with petrol up 23.6% and adding 0.77 points. Electricity was up 12.8% and rents were up 3.6%. The cash rate target is 4.85% after 5 rises in 2026, from 3.60% before the first rise. Mortgage repayments are not part of the grocery price index. The briefing notes point to the same watch list: petrol, power bills, housing, and the cash rate, ahead of the average supermarket aisle.
